key_insight: Quantum cost landscapes contain low-cost ravines that can be traced with NEB and exploited to build better variational quantum predictors.
engineering_relevance: The proposed ravine-aware ensemble strategy improves QNN/VQA prediction quality while lowering computation versus naive ensembling, making it attractive for resource-constrained quantum workflows.
method: Adapted nudged elastic band (NEB) to search between local minima in quantum cost landscapes.
Trained QNNs on concentratable entanglement classification for hardware-efficient ansatzes.
Ensembled predictions from models placed along the low-cost NEB path and used local-prediction variability as a pre-training metric.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that ravine-based QNN NEB ensembles outperform classical and naive quantum alternatives when starting from high local-prediction variability initializations, and that ravines persist under depth and qubit scaling.
watch_item: NEB ensemble gains depend on finding suitable low-variability ravine structure and may be less effective when the landscape does not exhibit clear low-cost paths.
paper_title: Ravines in quantum cost landscapes: opportunities for improved VQA predictions
